I've got several spare virtual servers laying around from random dev work and projects, in fact, I don't even use a proper VPN except to log into employee only areas of my workplace's website to access tools to do my job as I need to adjust routes in the ovpn file to only route work traffic over it. But when I do want to browse securely, on my own time, I don't use a proper VPN service or self-setup VPN either... Perhaps I should, but that's not what this is about.

What do I do? I use a tool called 'sshuttle'. You can read more about it here: https://github.com/apenwarr/sshuttle

Setting it up is extremely easy, which is why I prefer to use it over a traditional VPN client normally.

On yoour Linux destkop:

sudo apt-get install sshuttle -y

Simple install.

Now, how to connect? Equally simple:

sshuttle --dns -vvr [USER]@[IP-ADDRESS]:[SSH Port] 0/0

So for example:

sshuttle --dns -vvr john@123.45.67.08:19735 0/0

That would connect to the server with the IP 123.45.67.08 over SSH port 19735. More details regarding the other flags used int he command can be found here: https://github.com/apenwarr/sshuttle

That's it!

Go to http://geoiptool.com to confirm that your traffic is being routed over your VPS server.

It's basic, it's quick, it's easy. Are there more feature-rich options? Of course. This is just a barebones, quick and easy method of connecting to a remote Linux machine to tunnel your traffic through.
